title: Zilgit Snaps the Streak by 1.74, the Commish Drops 146, and Randy Cleans Out the Garage
dek: The rookie took down Team Pillbert as a 28% underdog, Sonny posted the week's top score by nearly 27 points, and the race for the top suddenly has three real contenders.
body: Five straight wins, a 5-1 record, and a 72% pregame edge, and Team Pillbert still could not get past the first-year manager. Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Alan's Team Pillbert 87.96 to 86.22, a 1.74-point upset that ended Philly's winning streak at five. The win came without help from Zilgit's top receiver: Nico Collins scored 1.6 on a 14.01 projection, the second-worst bust of the week. She won anyway, which is not how a rookie is supposed to handle a day when her WR1 disappears.

Alan's loss had an obvious culprit. Jalen Coker scored 1.4 on a 12.57 projection, the week's worst bust, and Justin Jefferson added just 6.4 in the lineup. Either one producing an ordinary afternoon covers a 1.74-point gap. Javonte Williams did his part with 21.5, but Phillibert's title odds fell from 26% to 17%, and the bad guy now has to regroup before the biggest game of Week 8.

The commish had the best day of anyone. Sonny's The Horse is Hea crushed Randy's The fumblers 146.72 to 108.52 as a road favorite, and the 146.72 beat the week's next-best score by 26.88 points. Jaxon Smith-Njigba scored 26.8 on a 16.25 projection, Bucky Irving added 23.5 on a 12.81 projection, and Jameson Williams, a waiver pickup from last week, posted 23.6 on an 8.95 projection. That trio combined for 73.9, and Sonny's title odds jumped from 11% to 28%, the biggest gain in the league. Randy got 22.12 from Caleb Williams, but Derrick Henry managed 5.4 on a 17.37 projection, his second straight week under six points. The fumblers have now lost four straight, and their playoff odds are down to 24%.

Kaushal's Habibsters beat Mekhi's Dawgs 119.84 to 93.58 in the 2-4 showdown, and the UGA man enjoyed a win over a team called Dawgs. Drake Maye scored 27.44 on a 20.59 projection, his second strong start since arriving off the wire. A Patriots quarterback is winning games for Habib while the commish, who has spent years soaking up Boston sports, is busy picking up Lamar Jackson. The scary part for the rest of the league is that Tony Pollard scored 35 on Kaushal's bench, the week's biggest bench blunder, and Habibsters still won by 26.26. For Kai, Tee Higgins put up 23.8 on the bench and Ashton Jeanty added 17.6 in the lineup. Mekhi is now 2-5 with 9% playoff odds.

Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 98 to 60.88 as an 85% favorite, and Brucie did it with 23.7 points from Zay Flowers sitting on his bench. JMoney had the best individual performance of the week: Joe Burrow scored 28.88 on a 19.31 projection. That leaves 32 points for the rest of the lineup, including 2.2 from Isaiah Likely and 4.2 from Denzel Boston. Burrow by himself scored almost half of Jordan's total. That math is cruel, and at 1-6 with 0% playoff odds, JMoney knows that math better than anyone.

Ramon still leads at 6-1 with 927.4 points, 73.8 ahead of anyone else, but for the second straight week a win cost him title odds, this time from 50% to 37%. Credit Sonny for that, as The Horse is Hea moved to 5-2 and 28%. Team Pillbert is also 5-2 at 17%. Habibsters hold the fourth seed at 3-4, and Kaushal's title odds more than doubled from 6% to 15%, with a 69% shot at the playoffs. Behind him, it's a crowded mess: The fumblers (24% playoff odds) and Ghostu-Spider SZN (6%) are also 3-4, Dawgs are 2-5 but at 9%, and Jordan is 1-6.

Sonny lived on the waiver wire. He swapped Patrick Mahomes for Lamar Jackson and Bryce Young for C.J. Stroud, replaced Cam Skattebo with Jordan Mason, added Zach Charbonnet, picked up Will Reichard for Terry McLaurin, and traded the 49ers D/ST for the Broncos D/ST. Emanuel Wilson somehow both left and came back during the same week. Randy cleaned house, cutting Jordan Addison, Alec Pierce, Darren Waller, Kenny Gainwell, and the Rams D/ST while adding Jaylin Noel, DeMario Douglas, Cameron Dicker, the Browns D/ST, and the Bears D/ST, the same defense the commish cut a week ago. Elsewhere, Ramon picked up Brandon Aubrey, whom Randy cut last week, Kai added Aaron Rodgers, Zoe swapped David Montgomery for Blake Corum, JMoney cut Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins, and Habib added Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker.

Week 8's headliner is Team Pillbert against The Horse is Hea, two 5-2 teams with second place on the line and a trade history that's still being debated. Kaushal and Zoe meet in a 3-4 matchup where Habib can strengthen his hold on fourth and Zilgit can try to make her 6% look silly. Randy hosts JMoney needing to stop a four-game slide, and Ramon takes on Kai, who needs an upset to keep his season alive. If Mekhi gets everyone in the right lineup slots, that one could be more interesting than the 6-1 vs 2-5 records suggest.

trade_watch.take: Last week this looked like a rout for Alan; this week it flipped. Pickens and Gordon started and scored 30.5 in Sonny's 146-point win, while Hubbard gave Philly 8 and Smith didn't start. Points since the deal are close now at 40.8 to 43.6, and they meet head to head next week.

Javonte keeps piling up points: 21.5 more this week and 75.5 since the deal, every one of them in Alan's lineup. Diggs didn't start for Randy and still has just 6 lineup points, during a four-game losing streak.

Jefferson's 6.4 in a 1.74-point loss is the stat that'll bother Philly, and he's now at 22.2 since the deal. Jeanty alone gave Kai 17.6 this week, so Mekhi's side leads 65.6 to 22.2, though the Dawgs lost too.

A quiet week for JMoney's haul: Likely 2.2 and Boston 4.2 in the lineup, Egbuka zero on the bench. Likely is still up to 50 since the deal, but the trade that won Jordan his only game didn't help him this week.

bios.1: The commish posted the week's top score, 146.72, and jumped from 11% to 28% in title odds, the league's biggest move. At 5-2 with a churned-up roster and a hot receiver room, The Horse is Hea is suddenly the top challenger. Next up is Philly, his old trade partner.
bios.2: Four straight losses, Derrick Henry under six points for the second straight week, and playoff odds down to 24%. Randy responded with a five-player purge and a new Bears D/ST. JMoney's visit next week is a must-win.
bios.3: Joe Burrow scored 28.88, the best individual total of the week, and Jordan still lost by 37 with a 60.88. At 1-6 with 0% playoff odds, JMoney is playing for pride now, and a struggling Randy is a fine place to start.
bios.4: A five-game win streak ended by 1.74 points against a 28% underdog, with Jalen Coker's 1.4 doing most of the damage. Still 5-2 with 94% playoff odds, but title odds slid to 17%. A matchup with the commish will show whether this was a blip.
bios.5: 2-5 after another week with big points on the bench, this time Tee Higgins' 23.8. Jeanty keeps producing and Aaron Rodgers just arrived, but 9% playoff odds leave no room for error. Next up is the league leader.
bios.6: Two straight wins, Drake Maye rolling, and the fourth seed at 3-4 with 69% playoff odds. Title odds more than doubled to 15%, and that was with 35 points stuck on the bench. The two-time champ has plenty of momentum.
bios.7: 6-1, 927.4 points, and a three-game win streak, with enough depth to leave 23.7 on the bench and still win by 37. Brucie still owns the best team in the league, even if the model keeps cutting his title odds, now 37%. Kai gets the next shot.
bios.8: The rookie took down a five-game winner by 1.74 even with her top receiver scoring 1.6. At 3-4 the model still gives her just 6% playoff odds, but she's tied in the standings with the fourth seed. Habib is next.
